delta.description: pixel-layer experiment on the GPT-4 vs AlphaMissense pair (closes the round-25 hole). Both PDFs rendered at 150 dpi (100 + 37 pages), pure-Python ink probe: GPT-4 report mean ink 0.0752, 703 bytes/word, pearson(words,bytes)=0.7354 (text-carried); AlphaMissense deck mean ink 0.4674 (6.2x), 27,274 bytes/word (38.8x), pearson=0.0772 (pixel-carried), 16:9 slides with full-bleed imagery (ink ~0.98 on 14 pages). The two documents carry meaning on different layers.

evidence.tool: trials/meaning-pair-round-02/probe_pixels.py (IHDR + zlib + PNG unfilter; white = all channels >= 240)

documented_holes: the pixel probe measures ink quantity, not figure content: what the figures say is still unread (no OCR on raster text, no figure classification)
white threshold 240 is a declared convention; antialiased edges are counted as ink
palette-type PNGs would be skipped (not encountered here)
no_claims: no claim about the figures' content or correctness
no claim that ink fraction equals meaning: it is a measured carrier-weight proxy
rendered PNGs and full texts stay local; pixel-probe.json aggregates may be disclosed
